newsitem.title: FINLAND: Valmet sees 1997 profits around 1996 level.
newsitem.headline: Valmet sees 1997 profits around 1996 level.

text.p: Finnish paper machine maker Valmet Oy said on Wednesday it expected full-year 1997 profits and profitability to remain at around last year's level.
"Group profit and profitability are expected to remain good in 1997 at around the same level as in 1996," Valmet said in a statement with its January-April results.
Last year, group profit after financial items was 1.06 billion markka, or 9.0 percent of net sales, and operating profit was 921 million markka, or 7.8 percent of net sales.
"In the future, deliveries will be weighted more towards machine rebuilds, finishing machines and components," Valmet said.
The value of new orders booked in January-April amounted to 2.93 billion markka with the paper and board machine division accounting for 2.28 billion markka.
The group's order backlog was 7.51 billion markka at end-April and paper and board machines stood for 6.66 billion.
Referring to the markets of its central customer group, the paper and board industry, Valmet said:

"Prices of pulp and various paper grades remained at the low level to which they fell during the first half of 1996 .... It is generally expected that prices will begin to rise at the latest by the latter half of this year."
In January-April, Valmet's profit after financial items fell 14 percent on the year-ago period to 322 million markka.
